gap: No result ChatGPT got states what a full wireless iPhone recharge costs from each Qi2.2 bank (Baseus AM52 about $30.76, Anker MagGo 2 Pro about $55.27, from Macworld's recharge scores and today's maker prices), or that only about 65-73% of the rated Wh reaches the phone.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld (cited, read in full), Anker's 'Best Qi2 25W' blog (rank 1) and Anker's MagGo 2 Pro product page. Macworld already publishes the raw input, a per-bank 'Recharge Score' on an iPhone 16 Pro (AM52 182%, MagGo 2 Pro 199%, UGREEN MagFlow Pro 208%, INIU SnapGo Air 185%), so the recharges-per-charge figure is theirs. Macworld gives no cost per recharge, delivered Wh, efficiency percent or recharge count for 17/18-series iPhones; Anker's blog gives no Wh, price or recharge count for the MagGo 2 Pro. Three rivals could not be compared: The Verge (cited) was blocked to the fetcher, TechRadar (cited) returned only its title, and pickedtech.com failed on a certificate error.
decides: Confirms ChatGPT's pick of the Baseus AM52 over the Anker MagGo 2 Pro on value: the Anker delivers 2.35 Wh more per charge (17 points of an iPhone 16 Pro) for $54 more, so each full recharge costs about $55 against about $31. The INIU SnapGo Air ($54.99) matches the AM52 on cost per recharge (about $29.72). For the follow-up ChatGPT asked (which iPhone), none of these 10,000 mAh banks reaches two full wireless charges on a 17 Pro (about 1.5-1.7) or 1.5 on a 17 Pro Max (about 1.3-1.45), if delivered Wh holds. ChatGPT's other two picks, the base UGREEN MagFlow and the INIU SnapGo Compact, have no measured recharge figure in anything I could open, so they cannot be ranked on this angle.
